name: X-phase through an H-box
summary: An X-phase on a leg of a standard H-box turns into a labelled H-box on the other legs.
description:
An X-spider with phase $\alpha$ on one leg of a standard H-box can be pushed through the H-box. On the other side it becomes an H-box with label $e^{i\alpha}$, connected to Z-spiders on all the remaining legs. The reason is that an H-box followed by a Hadamard on one leg is an AND gate, and an X-rotation before a Hadamard is a Z-rotation after it; a Z-phase on the output of an AND gate is a multiply-controlled phase, which is exactly what an H-box with label $e^{i\alpha}$ on copies of the inputs represents.

Shown for an H-box with three legs; it holds for any number of legs.
parameter_notes: n is the number of other legs of the H-box (shown for n = 2); holds for any n.
notes: The H-boxes here are *unnormalised*: an H-box with label $a$ has all entries equal to $1$, except for the entry where all wires are $1$, which is $a$. The grey spiders of the ZH papers are normalised differently from the X-spiders of PyZX, so scalar factors may differ from those in the papers.
